name: Ferrari 335 S Spider Scaglietti
description:
The last and largest of Ferrari's four-cam sports V12s: 4.0 litres, some 390 hp, in a Scaglietti spider weighing under 900 kg. Four were built for 1957.

A 335 S is the reason the Mille Miglia no longer exists. On 12 May 1957, ten kilometres past Guidizzolo and near the end of the race, a tyre let go on the car of Alfonso de Portago. He, his navigator Edmund Nelson and nine spectators, five of them children, were killed. Italy banned road racing, and the twenty-fourth Mille Miglia was the last.

The type went on to win the Swedish Grand Prix and the Venezuelan Grand Prix that same year, and took Ferrari the 1957 World Sportscar Championship.
